The growth bet

GROWTH HYPOTHESIS

FinWise's biggest growth challenge is its low Trial-to-Paid conversion (1.99%), suggesting users aren't experiencing enough product value.

SLIDE 7 · THE MECHANIC04 / 08

From first value to habit

THE MECHANIC · MODULE 3

Five invoices in the first 30 days

I chose a progress bar tied to creating five invoices within the first 30 days because this behavior has been identified as predictive of retention.

The mechanic combines educational triggers, visible progress, and meaningful rewards that reinforce business value.

THE HABIT LOOP

Education → Visible progress → Investment & return

Saved customer details and recurring invoices create reasons to return.

Open prototype ↗
VIEW COMPLETE SOURCE CONTENT +
- Mechanic + rationale: Module 3 · Retention & Engagement. The engagement mechanic that builds the habit loop, with rationale and a wireframe. For FinWise, users might not know how to create invoices or realize how much time they could save by automating them. So, this is also an educational trigger so the action can be a recurring task if they know how to use it. I chose a progress bar tied to creating five invoices within the first 30 days because this behavior has been identified as predictive of retention. The mechanic combines educational triggers to teach users how to invoice, visible progress to encourage repeated usage, and meaningful rewards that reinforce business value. By saving customer details and scheduling recurring invoices, users invest in FinWise, making future actions easier and creating contextual reasons to return. - Wireframe link: https://trueframe-ui-capture.lovable.app/

SLIDE 9 · THE VALIDATION06 / 08

Validate the activation bet

METHOD · MULTI-ARMED BANDIT3 ARMSTARGET · +15% IMPORT COMPLETION
HYPOTHESIS

If we introduce a personalized onboarding experience that guides FinWise trial users toward importing their financial data and discovering value through collaboration, we expect more users to reach their first Aha Moment, as measured by an increase in the Data Import completion rate (%).

EXPERIMENT · ACTIVATION DURING ONBOARDING
ARM 01Questionnaire

Before import

ARM 02Video tutorial

Before import

ARM 03Checklist

Shared with teammates

MINI EXPERIMENT BRIEF

Primary metric: weekly Import completion rate, target: A 15% increase of import completion rate

Guardrail: Onboarding completion rate (sign-up → dashboard) must not drop by more than 2 percentage points versus the current flow.

Read date: in the next 2-3 weeks (Trial will need to finish to also see the impact)

Why Multi-Armed Bandit? As we cannot afford conversion loss and we need a result in the next 2-3 weeks to impact conversion. We assume the algorithm and the tech are implemented.

Traffic allocation: minimum 1% to 5% of traffic per arm.

VIEW COMPLETE SOURCE CONTENT +
- Method + why: **Method:** Multi-Armed Bandit**Why:** For this experiment, as we cannot afford conversion loss and we need a result in the next 2-3 weeks to impact conversion we prefer to go with a Multi-Armed Bandit. We assume we have the algorithm and the tech implemented to run it.**Traffic allocation:** minimum 1% to 5% of traffic per arm, so no arm is starved before the bandit has enough data. - Hypothesis + primary metric: If we introduce a personalized onboarding experience that guides FinWise trial users toward importing their financial data and discovering value through collaboration, we expect more users to reach their first Aha Moment, as measured by an increase in the Data Import completion rate (%). **Primary metric:** weekly Import completion rate, target: A 15% increase of import completion rate **Experiment:** Activation during onboarding test. Show the core value of FinWise during onboarding and be able to move the metric from Trial to Paid. **Testing 3 arms.** Showing: 1. Questionnaire before import 2. Video tutorial before import 3. Checklist and shared with teammates Always in a base of collaboration on Trial users. **Current experience:** onboarding now is asking just to import after registration. **Predicted outcome:** We predict that the Data Import completion rate will increase over the next two weeks, leading to an improvement in Trial-to-Paid conversion over time. **If successful:** If a prompt variant wins, we will adopt it and run a follow-up experiment to further improve activation and Trial-to-Paid conversion. For example: - **Video wins:** Test different video content or messaging. - **Questionnaire wins:** Test different personalization questions. - **Checklist wins:** Test different checklist steps or sequences. The goal is to iteratively optimize the winning experience and measure whether each improvement drives higher Data Import completion and, ultimately, Trial-to-Paid conversion. **If unsuccessful:** Review where users start but fail to complete the data import process, identify any errors or friction points, and reassess whether collaboration is the right approach to helping users experience product value. If the hypothesis is not validated, explore an alternative growth loop and run a follow-up experiment to test its impact on activation and Trial-to-Paid conversion. - Guardrail + read date: - **Guardrail:** Onboarding completion rate (sign-up → dashboard) must not drop by more than 2 percentage points versus the current flow.- **Read date:** in the next 2-3 weeks (Trial will need to finish to also see the impact)

SLIDE 10 · THE MODEL07 / 08

Protect the value. Then price it.

STAGE 1 · VALUE CREATIONMODEL · FREEMIUMREVERSE TRIAL
RECOMMENDATION

FinWise should stay with the reverse trial + freemium model for now.

It's not the time to change, because FinWise first needs to improve how users understand the product's value. Once that's solved, it can invest extra resources in testing a pricing change.

THE PRICING BET

We believe that offering full Premium access during the reverse trial, followed by a limited free plan, will increase activation and willingness to pay by allowing users to experience the value of automation and collaboration before committing to a subscription.

THE SUPPORTING SIGNALS
1
Bank connection completion rate
2
Invoice creation completion rate
3
Automation completion rate
4
Dashboard views

Only 2% of trial users convert, and 40% are retained after one year. Full Premium access during the reverse trial lets users experience value before committing.

VIEW COMPLETE SOURCE CONTENT +
- Growth stage + model: **Stage:** Stage 1 · Value Creation. Reaching $10M isn’t enough if users aren’t experiencing FinWise’s value. FinWise is spending heavily on acquisition while failing to convert trial users into paying customers or retain them over time. Only 2% of trial users convert, and 40% are retained after one year.**Model:** Freemium. It builds a large pool of user data, behavioral insights, low CAC and strong network effects, rather than a highly predictable upsell pool. With a reverse-trial model, the challenge is deciding which features remain free while ensuring users experience enough value to stay engaged and recognize the additional benefits of upgrading to Premium. - Recommendation + bet: FinWise should stay with the reverse trial + freemium model for now. It's not the time to change, because FinWise first needs to improve how users understand the product's value. Once that's solved, it can invest extra resources in testing a pricing change. **The pricing bet:** We believe that offering full Premium access during the reverse trial, followed by a limited free plan, will increase activation and willingness to pay by allowing users to experience the value of automation and collaboration before committing to a subscription. - Supporting signal: Bank connection completion rate, invoice creation completion rate, automation completion rate and dashboard views. Our priority is to drive activation by allowing users to experience FinWise's full value during the reverse trial. After the trial, essential features, automatic bank synchronization and historical transactions remain free, so users keep reaching the Aha moment. Collaboration with teammates and advanced automation, such as recurring invoices and advanced reporting, require a paid subscription.

SLIDE 11 · THE STORY + SUBMIT08 / 08

What changed my thinking

BIGGEST FRICTION

The correlation data in the exercise didn't show all the details we needed. I understood this was intentional, to show us ambiguity, so I used the information I had and made assumptions where needed, as can happen in real life.

KEY AHA MOMENT

I thought growth loops were only useful for acquisition. Using one for activation was a real Aha moment, because it gave the exercise a different angle and more creativity.

COURSE TAKEAWAYS

Experiments like A/B tests can take longer than expected when you need a quick result, so we need other ways to test a hypothesis, such as a Multi-Armed Bandit test.

READY TO SUBMIT
